image_description: A grey whale swimming in the ocean near a boat with tourists. The whale's back and head are visible above the water surface, showing characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. A spout of water is visible from its blowholes. Several people on the boat are observing and photographing the whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears consistent with a grey whale, showing the characteristic arched rostrum. The blowhole area is visible with the spout indicating proper placement.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin shows the characteristic mottled grey coloration with lighter patches that appear to be barnacles/whale lice.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No dorsal fin is visible, and the back shows the characteristic series of small humps/knuckles typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows the robust, thick build characteristic of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with head checkpoints, the body skin shows appropriate mottling and barnacle patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's mouth is not open and baleen plates are internal/not visible from this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are submerged and not visible in this image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are not visible in this image as only the front/mid section of the whale is shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin texture appears rough with the characteristic bumps/callosities associated with barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The barnacle patches appear slightly uniform in distribution and texture, lacking the random variation seen in real whale photography. Some patches blend too smoothly into the skin.
The water spout has an overly soft, painterly quality rather than the crisp droplet structure expected in high-speed photography of whale blows.
Slight inconsistency in the boat railing geometry and passenger proportions suggest minor perspective issues common in AI generation.
